$NMR traded 11.2 times its 7-day average volume in the last 24 hours. That is about 24.2M USDT, and it is the number I care about most here.

Price is 12.77, up 16% on the day and 32.6% on the week. But it reached 15.5 this week and now sits 17.6% below that high. Hourly RSI is 53, so the heat has already left the move.

This is not a market-wide push. $BTC is down 0.87% over the same 24 hours. Buyers came for this coin specifically.

My view: no trade yet. A spike on huge volume followed by a quick fade often leaves late buyers stuck near the top. The chart shows most of this week's gain came in one burst.

What would change my mind:
A move back above 15.5 with volume still far above average. Then the breakout is real and I turn bullish.
On the other side, a close below 12.36, the middle of the 7-day range (9.21 to 15.5), and I expect more of the gain to fade.

Sentiment sits in Greed at 73. In that mood I would rather wait for proof than chase.

Next I watch the volume on the next push up. If it holds, the move has support. If it dries up, the fade is the more likely path.

Decrypt reports that Bitcoin ETFs have now seen inflows for eight straight days, adding about $2.95B over 30 days as they bounced back from the Clarity Act sell-off.

That reads bullish. The $BTC price does not agree yet.

Price is 83,695, down 2.9% on the week and flat on the day at -0.17%. It sits 4.1% under the 7-day high of 87,279. Volume is at 0.8 times its 7-day average, so trading activity is below normal despite the headlines.

My read: the inflows are soaking up selling, not driving a move. That is support, but support is not a trend. Hourly RSI at 51 says momentum is neutral.

One more thing bothers me. Fear & Greed shows 73, Greed, while price is lower on the week. Sentiment is running ahead of the chart.

View: no trade yet.
Above 87,279 with volume back above average, the flows are finally showing up in price and I turn bullish.
Below 82,563, the 7-day low, the inflows are not enough and I expect more downside.

What I watch next: whether the inflow streak holds while price stays in this range, and which side of it breaks first.

$QNT is up 271% in seven days. It ran from a 7-day low of 69.4 to a high of 373 and now trades at 272.66.

The detail I keep coming back to is volume. 24h turnover is about 153.9M USDT, 1.9 times the 7-day average. That average already includes the whole run, so buyers have not left yet.

It also added 15.6% in the last 24 hours while $BTC moved only 0.35%. This is its own story, not the market lifting everything.

Still, price sits 26.9% below the 373 high, and the chart shows that spike was short and sold off hard. Hourly RSI at 61 is warm, not extreme.

My view: I respect the strength, but I will not chase a coin that is up 271% in a week. No trade yet.

What would make me bullish: a hold above 373 with volume still near 2x its average.
What would make me cautious: a drop back under about 236, where price stood 24 hours ago. That erases today's gain and points to fading demand.

Fear & Greed at 73 says the crowd is already leaning in. Next I watch whether volume holds on the next test of the highs.

On most days, $BTC sets the direction for the whole market. Today shows both sides of that rule.

The drag. Bitcoin is the biggest and most traded coin. When it moves hard, traders tend to move the rest with it, so large altcoins often follow its direction, usually with bigger swings.

Look at the majors now. BTC is flat, up 0.06% in 24 hours. ETH is up 0.35% and SOL 0.04%. BNB is the odd one at -1.07%. When Bitcoin goes nowhere, the big coins mostly go nowhere too.

The decoupling. A coin breaks away when it has its own reason to move. $AAVE is up 12.4% and $HBAR is down 14.8% on a day when BTC barely changed. Neither move came from Bitcoin.

How to check it: compare the coin's move with BTC over the same window. If BTC is flat and the coin moves 10% or more, the move is about the coin. Then look at volume. AAVE traded about 73M USDT and HBAR about 97M, so real money sat behind both.

One caveat. These solo moves usually last only while BTC stays calm. Right now it is calm: 4.2% under its 7-day high, hourly RSI near 50. A sharp BTC move tends to pull everything back in line.

Practical takeaway: before trading an altcoin, check what BTC did in the same period. It tells you if you are trading the coin or just the market.

The first US spot $NEAR ETF went live today, and NEAR volume came in below its weekly average. That gap is my whole take.

Per Decrypt, Bitwise's NRR started trading on NYSE Arca on Tuesday. It gives brokerage accounts NEAR exposure plus staking rewards, after the token nearly tripled since August.

Now the market data. Price is 4.926, up 4.2% on the day and 12.2% on the week. But it sits 11.7% under the 7-day high of 5.578. Spot volume was about 202.7M USDT, only 0.74 times the 7-day average. Hourly RSI is 51, neutral.

A launch like this is the kind of news traders position for in advance. When the day arrives and volume drops instead of rising, I read it as the news already being priced in. It is not bearish on its own, but it is not a fresh buyer showing up either.

View: no trade yet.
A move back above 5.578 on volume above average would tell me ETF demand is real, and I turn bullish.
Below 4.80, the middle of this week's range, I expect a classic sell-the-news fade.

$BTC is flat at +0.12%, so NEAR has to carry this move alone. Next I watch whether volume picks up over the next few sessions.
